text.subject: Your published email depends on a domain approaching expiry
body: A domain you use for your published email is approaching expiry. If it lapses, quote requests and bank letters sent to that address will bounce.

Your strong customer rating helps householders shortlist you, but an unanswered low review leaves them unsure whether the problem was resolved. Your contractor grade also differs across public sources, potentially limiting the contracts you can bid for.

titles.f2: Forged payment-change emails could reach your clients, suppliers or bank under your name.
titles.f3: Your contractor portfolio is empty, leaving tender panels without projects to score.
titles.f4: Your company profile's broken phone field leaves buyers unable to reach you by tapping call.
titles.f5: An unanswered low review leaves householders unsure whether the problem was resolved.
titles.f6: A search check flags your site's robots file, which can keep new pages out of search results.
titles.f7: Missing security headers can expose visitors on untrusted networks and trigger client IT checks.
titles.f8: Missing company and authorship signals may send assistants to outdated directories.
titles.f9: Missing contact and privacy links can weaken your credibility with banks and procurement officers.
titles.f10: Your pages give AI assistants little to quote when buyers seek solar contractors.
titles.f14: Missing structured details make competitors easier for search engines and AI assistants to quote.
titles.c1: Your head office unit differs across 3 sources, risking customers and couriers going to the wrong door.
titles.c2: Your main phone number differs across 3 sources, leaving buyers unsure which line reaches your office.

titles.c5: Your office lists differ across 2 sources, so customers may assume you cannot serve them.
titles.c6: Your project totals differ across 2 sources, potentially weakening the experience a panel scores.
titles.c7: Your legal form differs across 2 sources, leaving clients and banks seeing different entities.
titles.c8: Your contractor grade differs across 2 sources, potentially limiting the contracts you can bid for.
titles.c9: Your energy totals differ across 2 sources, leaving customers and tender panels unsure which is current.
titles.n1: A cluster of high ratings on one day may be worth checking.
titles.n2: Your site's limited archive record may be worth checking.
titles.n3: Your published capacity and revenue claims may be worth checking against outside sources.
titles.n4: An office listed without a street address or phone number may be worth checking.
